newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Westpac Australia leading index rises in Nov.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Westpac Australia leading index rises in Nov.

text.p: The Westpac-Melbourne Institute leading index of Australian economic activity, which indicates where activity will be in six to nine months time, rose by 0.9 points or 0.6 percent in November, Westpac said.
It said the coincident index, which measures current economic activity, rose 2.8 points or 1.6 percent in November.

The leading index of inflation rose slightly in November to 4.9 precent from 4.5 percent in October but continued to suggest only moderate inflation pressures, Westpac's general manager of economic strategy and planning, Bill Evans, said in a statement.
The six month smoothed annual growth rate of the leading index rose to 3.4 percent in November, the first time it has been above its long term trend since October 1994.
The smoothed growth rate, which Evans said was the best guide to future activity, had been mostly in a range of zero to 2.6 percent through 1996.
Evans said the leading index had been affected by sharp rise in non-residential construction approvals, relating to a number of Olympic Games projects valued at over A$450 million.

"While Olympic related projects will provide a boost to the economy, their specific impact on the leading index for November has been to send a stronger signal than is appropriate," he said. He said that without the Olympic factor, the smooth annual growth rate would have been around two percent.
"That caution aside, the steady trend rise in the leading index is consistent with our view that the economy will start to grow more strongly by late 1997," he said in a statement.

Despite this, Evans said given the slow pace of current activity indicated by the coincident index, the likelihood of good inflation numbers next week, and pressure on the government to pare back fiscal spending, there was a strong case for a further final interest rate cut in the March quarter.
The slight rise in the leading index of inflation only suggested moderate inflationary pressures, he said.
Underlying inflation looked set to stay at the low end of the Reserve Bank's target band through 1997, Evans said.
Westpac is forecasting next week's December quarter inflation data to show an annual underlying rate of 2.1 percent, and an annual rise in the consumer price index of 1.6 percent.
